lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Decision Analysis and Expected Value Capstone
lessonRef.title: Guided practice A: weighing expected value against risk

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Use this example as the model for the guided set below.

items.prompt: Costs $5, pays $40 with probability 1/10. Expected value?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: An insurer charges a premium of $12 and pays out $216 with probability 1/36. Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.
Option A has expected payoff $22 and Option B has expected payoff $27. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option B; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.
Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.
Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between two people using a single fair coin flip.
choices: Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.
Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.
Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.

items.prompt: A game costs $10 to play. It pays $120 with probability 1/10 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $12; the game is favourable to the player
$-10; the game is unfavourable to the player
$110; the game is favourable to the player
$2; the game is favourable to the player

items.prompt: An insurer charges a premium of $4 and pays out $261 with probability 1/87. Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Option A has expected payoff $5 and Option B has expected payoff $22. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option B; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.
Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between three people by rolling a standard die, assigning two faces to each.
choices: Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.
Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.
Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.

items.prompt: A game costs $22 to play. It pays $228 with probability 1/19 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $206; the game is favourable to the player
$-10; the game is unfavourable to the player
$-22; the game is unfavourable to the player
$12; the game is favourable to the player
